items.title: Heredoc bodies written to a file are dropped from the judged text

criteria.text: A heredoc body that a command only writes to a file (cat or tee with a redirect) is left out of the text before the deny patterns, the push rule and the sensitive-path scan run, so prose in the body is not judged as a command line.
A heredoc fed to a shell or an interpreter (bash, sh, zsh, node, python and the like) is still scanned in full.

items.title: Push deny pattern and push rule match within one line

criteria.text: The git push deny pattern in the profile and the push rule in the git guard match within a single line, so words on later lines of a command do not count as push arguments.
A test in tests/ covers each case: a cat heredoc, a tee heredoc, a heredoc fed to a shell, a heredoc fed to an interpreter, and a push command followed by prose on another line.

items.title: rules.md row for command lines, not prose

criteria.text: docs/rules.md has a row stating that the Bash guard judges command lines, not prose, with the failure that motivated it.
